title: Transitions Hiring Program — standing pool for recent graduates
org: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality · statewide, TX
location: Statewide, Texas (one application feeds vacancies agency-wide)
benefits: State of Texas employee benefits — health, retirement, paid leave
metaLine: Open to Dec 27 · $53,448 · a pool built specifically for recent grads with little or no experience
body: TCEQ's standing candidate pool specifically for recent college graduates holding an undergraduate or graduate degree and little or no work experience, used to fill agency-wide entry-level positions requiring only a bachelor's. One application feeds multiple vacancies statewide. Job ID 100072, posted agency-wide.
desc: This programme exists precisely for candidates in her position — a recent BS with minimal experience — which removes the experience barrier that screens her out of most state professional postings. One application covers vacancies across the whole agency, making it the single highest-leverage Texas submission on this site.

title: Natural Resources Specialist III — Water Quality Assessment Unit
org: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality · Water Quality Assessment Unit · Austin, TX
benefits: State of Texas employee benefits — health, retirement, paid leave
metaLine: Closes Aug 19 · $60,528 · builds the state's 303(d) impaired-waters list — her capstone at state scale
body: A position in TCEQ's Water Quality Assessment Unit, which produces the state's Integrated Report and the 303(d) impaired waters list. The work involves compiling and analysing surface water quality monitoring data, applying assessment methodology, and documenting waterbody status. Job ID 102332.
desc: Determining whether a waterbody is impaired, from monitoring data, is exactly what her Pigeon River trace-metal capstone did for one river — this does it for an entire state under the Clean Water Act. Of all the state-agency roles found this run, this is the closest analogue to the work she has already published.

title: Aquatic Resource Technician — Lake Mead National Recreation Area
org: American Conservation Experience (ACE EPIC) with the National Park Service · Boulder City, NV
url_label: ACE EPIC — Lake Mead aquatic resource technician
benefits: Public Land Corps eligibility — confers non-competitive federal hiring eligibility on completion
metaLine: Closes Aug 17 · $1,000/wk — the best-paid service placement found · PLC federal hiring eligibility
body: An individual placement with the NPS aquatic resources programme at Lake Mead National Recreation Area, supporting water resource monitoring and aquatic habitat work on the Colorado River system. Public Land Corps eligibility is required, which confers non-competitive federal hiring eligibility on completion.
desc: Two things make this stand out: it is the best-paid service placement found anywhere this run, and the Public Land Corps authority converts a completed term directly into non-competitive federal hiring eligibility — which is the hiring authority she should be collecting while her Recent Graduates window is still open.

title: Environmental Technician, Levels 1–3 (remote options)
org: Arizona Department of Environmental Quality · Phoenix, Chandler, Flagstaff, Scottsdale, Tempe, Tucson, AZ
location: Phoenix, Chandler, Flagstaff, Scottsdale, Tempe and Tucson, Arizona (remote-work flexibility)
url_label: Arizona State Jobs — ADEQ Environmental Technician
deadline: Open until filled — apply any time
benefits: State of Arizona employee benefits · remote-work flexibility
metaLine: Open until filled · $44,000–$65,000 · Level 1 accepts 0 years of experience · remote options
body: An ADEQ technician role handling permit application intake, technical review and data entry in state environmental databases, tracking compliance deadlines and coordinating with developers and engineering firms. Level 1 explicitly accepts zero to three years of experience, or a bachelor's in environmental sciences, hydrology, geology or chemistry. Open until filled with remote-work flexibility.
desc: Level 1 is written for a fresh environmental science BS with no required experience, which makes it one of the cleanest entry doors on this whole site. The open-until-filled posting and remote flexibility also mean she can apply now without it competing for time against a hard deadline elsewhere.

title: Environmental Science Specialist — Groundwater Inspector
org: Arizona Department of Environmental Quality · Water Quality Division · Phoenix, AZ
location: Phoenix, Arizona (statewide travel; roughly 60% office, 40% field)
url_label: Arizona State Jobs — ADEQ Groundwater Inspector
deadline: Open until filled — apply any time
metaLine: Open until filled · $45,000–$50,000 at Level 1 · groundwater protection inspections statewide
body: Conducts groundwater-protection inspections at industrial facilities, mines, wastewater treatment plants and collection systems across Arizona, drafts compliance and enforcement documentation, and works with permitted facilities to resolve Aquifer Quality Limit exceedances. Roughly 60% office and 40% field with overnight travel. Hired at Levels 1 through 3.
desc: Groundwater and water-quality compliance sits directly on her stated interest track, and Level 1 is the entry rung of the series. Mine inspections in particular connect to her trace-metal background — that is where metals enter groundwater in the first place.

title: Wildlife Technicians (statewide) — cougar trail cameras and small mammals
org: New Mexico Department of Game and Fish · statewide, based Santa Fe, NM
location: Statewide, New Mexico (based in Santa Fe)
url_label: TAMU board — NM Game and Fish 117761
benefits: Confirm the appointment terms with the department
metaLine: Closes Aug 14 · $180/day · cougar trail-camera monitoring AND small-mammal work — her two strongest skills
body: A field technician working alongside New Mexico Department of Game and Fish biologists on projects statewide across many terrestrial taxa — birds, carnivores, furbearers, small mammals and ungulates. Potential projects include cougar trail-camera monitoring, black bear hair-snare sampling, turkey trapping, prairie chicken tracking and bighorn sheep captures, plus periodic data entry.
desc: Cougar trail-camera monitoring and small-mammal work are literally her two strongest documented field skills — camera traps via Wildlife Insights and small-mammal trapping. She would be productive on day one rather than being trained up, which is exactly the argument to make in the application.

title: Biologist 1 (Seasonal) — Game Division
org: Nevada Department of Wildlife · Elko, NV
benefits: State of Nevada employee benefits — seasonal-status permanent appointment
metaLine: Rolling · $52,200–$76,608 · BIOLOGIST title · bachelor's-only minimum, NO experience required
body: A seasonal-status permanent NDOW position assisting Area Biologists with big game and upland game surveys by helicopter, ground and ATV, serving as a primary regional flight crew member. The role also covers private-land elk monitoring, fencing projects, damage assessments and trap, transplant and collaring efforts. The minimum qualification is a bachelor's in biology or wildlife management with no experience required.
desc: State biologist series openings almost always demand experience; this one explicitly does not, which makes it one of the very few genuinely open to a 2025 graduate. It also carries the biologist title rather than technician, at a salary starting above $52,000.

title: Biologist 2 (Underfill) — Biodiversity Division
org: Nevada Department of Wildlife · Biodiversity Division · Fallon, NV
metaLine: Rolling · $59,257–$87,570 · UNDERFILL — designed to appoint someone below the stated grade and promote them
body: A non-game wildlife management position in NDOW's Biodiversity Division working across mammals, birds, bats and reptiles on surveys, monitoring and management actions tied to the State Wildlife Action Plan. It is advertised as an underfill, meaning a candidate who does not yet meet Biologist 2 qualifications can be appointed at the lower level and progress upward.
desc: The underfill structure is the point here — it exists specifically to bring in someone at her exact experience level and promote them into the full class, so she should not self-screen on the Biologist 2 title. The small-mammal, bat and camera-survey work matches her skills directly.

title: Biological Technician — Desert National Wildlife Refuge (USFWS)
org: Great Basin Institute in cooperation with U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service · Las Vegas, NV
location: Las Vegas, Nevada (Desert National Wildlife Refuge)
benefits: Confirm the benefit package with Great Basin Institute
metaLine: Closes Aug 19 · GIS/GPS + restoration + monitoring, inside a USFWS refuge · BS with NO experience required
body: A Research Associate position with Great Basin Institute in cooperation with USFWS, supporting invasive species management, native habitat restoration, biological monitoring, volunteer stewardship and environmental outreach at Desert National Wildlife Refuge. Duties include collecting and managing field data and using GPS and GIS technologies. A bachelor's is required with no prior experience needed.
desc: This pairs GIS and GPS work with restoration and monitoring and places her inside a USFWS refuge programme — her target agency — with an explicit zero-experience requirement. GBI placements are also a well-documented bridge into permanent federal positions.

title: Wildlife Technician — Packsaddle Wildlife Management Area
org: Oklahoma Department of Wildlife Conservation · Packsaddle WMA, OK
pay: $51,584.00 per year plus state benefit allowance
benefits: State of Oklahoma benefit allowance — confirm the package with the department
metaLine: Closes Aug 14 · $51,584 permanent · one assignment track is explicitly wetland infrastructure
body: A full-time technician working under a wildlife biologist on surveys, inventories, habitat development and WMA management. Depending on assignment, the role covers big game surveys, waterfowl and migratory bird work, Oklahoma Land Access Program habitat monitoring, or wetland infrastructure. Includes data collection, reporting and public assistance.
desc: A permanent state wildlife technician job at over $51,000 is already strong for an entry role, and one of the named assignment tracks is wetland infrastructure — which is where her delineation and survey experience would apply most directly. Worth stating that preference explicitly in the application.

title: Vegetation Monitoring Botany Assistant — NPS Sonoran Desert Network
org: Conservation Legacy with National Park Service Inventory & Monitoring · Tucson, AZ
url_label: TAMU board — Conservation Legacy / NPS I&M 117670
benefits: AmeriCorps education award eligible · no housing provided
metaLine: Closes Aug 14 · $870/wk for ~52 weeks · federal I&M monitoring protocols · Ed Award eligible
body: An approximately 52-week AmeriCorps position working alongside the NPS Inventory and Monitoring team in Tucson on long-term vegetation monitoring protocols across Sonoran Desert parks. The work includes field data collection, plant identification and data management. Education award eligible; no housing is provided.
desc: A full year working inside federal Inventory and Monitoring protocols is unusually good preparation for both graduate school and NPS or USFWS hiring, because those protocols are the standard the agencies actually use. She already has three Conservation Legacy applications in, so the organisation knows her name.

title: Field Technician — Conservation (entry-level, permanent)
org: Center for Environmental Health Monitoring and Management (CEHMM) · Carlsbad, NM
location: Carlsbad, New Mexico (southern New Mexico field sites)
benefits: Confirm the benefit package with CEHMM
metaLine: Open to Oct 31 · $22–$27/hr · full-time PERMANENT and explicitly entry-level · surveys + mapping
body: A full-time permanent, explicitly entry-level position supporting CEHMM's Lesser Prairie-Chicken and Dunes Sagebrush Lizard conservation programmes in southern New Mexico. Duties include biological surveys, habitat management, species monitoring, data entry and mapping. No prior experience is required.
desc: Permanent and explicitly entry-level is a rare pairing — most entry conservation work is seasonal. The combination of survey fieldwork and mapping fits her skills, and both target species are high-profile listed-species programmes that would read well on a later federal application.
